answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that grows with the number of identities it claims, so creating many fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Verification adds proof of useful work: an agent must complete small verifiable tasks before it can trade, like a marble rolling only after a push. Reputation earned over time acts as a horizon: new identities start with zero trust and build it gradually, while a walnut-hard rule slashes the stake of any identity caught submitting fake attestations, making mass fakery unprofitable.
